1. (Currently amended) A method, comprising: transmitting a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a first pulse rate to a vehicle; receiving a second sequence of modulated infrared light pulses from the vehicle; and transmitting a message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a second pulse rate based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first pulse rate is different from the second pulse rate, and wherein the message encodes vehicle safety information including vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status as binary bits independent of the pulse rate.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein a computing device determines the second pulse rate based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, the second pulse rate being slower than the first pulse rate to accommodate vehicle proximity conditions.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity based on loss of the second sequence of light pulses and transmits a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a third pulse rate, wherein the third pulse rate is faster than the second pulse rate.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of modulated infrared light pulses from a third vehicle and adjusts the message transmission to a fourth pulse rate based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the third vehicle, wherein the fourth pulse rate is different from the second pulse rate and is determined by the slowest pulse rate among all received sequences.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation.

6. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed.

7. (Original) The method of claim 6, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

8. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received via an IR video sensor.

9. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from two or more vehicles.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 9, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a fourth pulse rate based on the sequences of light pulses, wherein the fourth pulse rate is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses received from the two or more vehicles.

11. (Currently amended) An apparatus, comprising: a processor; a memory, the memory storing instructions executable by the processor to: transmit a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a first pulse rate to a vehicle; receive a second sequence of modulated infrared light pulses from the vehicle; and transmit a message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a second pulse rate based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first pulse rate is different from the second pulse rate, and wherein the message encodes vehicle safety information including vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status as binary bits independent of the pulse rate.

12. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein a computing device determines the second pulse rate based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, the second pulse rate being slower than the first pulse rate to accommodate vehicle proximity conditions.

13. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 12, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity based on loss of the second sequence of light pulses and transmits a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a third pulse rate, wherein the third pulse rate is faster than the second pulse rate.

14. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 13, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of modulated infrared light pulses from a third vehicle and adjusts the message transmission to a fourth pulse rate based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the third vehicle, wherein the fourth pulse rate is different from the second pulse rate and is determined by the slowest pulse rate among all received sequences.

15. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation.

16. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed.

17. (Original) The apparatus of claim 16, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

18. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received via an IR video sensor.

19. (Original) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from one or more vehicles.

20. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 19, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a fourth pulse rate based on the sequences of light pulses, wherein the fourth pulse rate is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses received from the one or more vehicles.
